title: Best 100 Pint Dehumidifier (2026): 80- to 130-Pint Picks
h1: The Best 100-Pint Dehumidifiers for Big Basements and Whole Homes
dek: When a 50-pint portable is running nonstop and still losing, it's time for real capacity. Here's what a genuine 100-pint dehumidifier looks like — and what to skip.
description: The best 100 pint dehumidifiers for big basements and whole homes, plus 80-, 90- and 130-pint options, and why most 100-pint portables aren't what they seem.
intro: A genuine **100 pint dehumidifier** is a different class of machine from the portables in the big-box aisle. Nearly all of them are whole-house or commercial units, rated under the AHAM standard used for installed equipment, built with heavier coils and blowers, and designed to drain continuously through a hose or condensate line. They're the right tool for a large, damp basement, an encapsulated crawl space under a big home, or a house where one or two portables simply can't keep humidity under 50%.

They're also where marketing gets slippery. Plenty of budget portables are sold as 80-, 100- or even 140-pint machines on the strength of saturation numbers that bear little resemblance to the DOE 2019 rating. We compared real 80- to 130-pint units on rated capacity, coverage, efficiency, drainage, installation options and owner-reported reliability, and we explain how to spot the inflated labels.
topPicksLead: The **Aprilaire E100** is the best 100-pint dehumidifier for most homes: true whole-house capacity, top-tier efficiency, and the flexibility to run ducted or freestanding.

products.whyWeLoveIt: The E100 is the benchmark 100-pint unit. It can sit on its own in a big basement or be tied into the HVAC system to dry the whole house, and it does it with some of the best efficiency in its class.
products.performance: Its 100-pint rating is measured at 80°F and 60% humidity under AHAM conditions, and Aprilaire rates it for homes up to roughly 5,500 square feet. Owners commonly report that it replaces two or three portables, ends bucket duty for good and holds a steady humidity level through the summer. Install quality matters more than anything else in owner complaints, so choose your contractor carefully.

blocks.text: Those figures sum up the market. Mainstream portables top out around 50 pints under the current DOE test, which is run at a cool 65°F. Machines rated 80 pints and up are almost all installed or commercial units measured under warmer AHAM conditions — and a portable listed at 80 or 100 pints is usually quoting a saturation number. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains both standards.

We don't run a lab. We compare published AHAM and DOE capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, manufacturer coverage figures, installation manuals and warranty terms, and we check for CPSC recalls. Then we read owner and contractor reviews in volume to identify recurring problems: failing pumps, coil leaks, sensor drift and noisy blowers.
For this guide we only included units whose capacity claims hold up under a recognized standard. We ranked them on real capacity, efficiency, installation flexibility and long-term support.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 100-pint dehumidifier

items.label: A rating you can trust
items.text: Look for the AHAM or DOE figure on the spec sheet. Be wary of portables that only list a capacity at saturation (often 95°F and 90% humidity).

items.label: Continuous drainage
items.text: A 100-pint unit can produce gallons of water a day. You need a floor drain, sump or condensate pump — not a bucket.

items.label: Install options
items.text: Freestanding units are simplest; ducted units dry the whole house. Our [whole-house dehumidifier installation](/guides/whole-house-dehumidifier-installation/) guide covers both.

items.label: Efficiency
items.text: Big units run for hundreds of hours a season. An ENERGY STAR Most Efficient model saves real money over its life.

items.label: Low-temperature operation
items.text: For cool basements and crawl spaces, check the unit's defrost range and minimum operating temperature.

items.label: Warranty
items.text: Five to six years is typical for quality whole-house units — well beyond the one to two years on most portables.

blocks.text: Since the DOE changed its test in 2019, portable ratings dropped across the board because units are now measured at 65°F instead of 80°F. Reputable brands relabeled their 70-pint models as 50-pint models. Some budget sellers went the other way, advertising saturation figures that make a modest machine look enormous.

blocks.text: If you're searching for an Aprilaire 1850 or 1852, you're looking at Aprilaire's older 95-pint whole-house models. The current E-series — E080, E100 and E130 — fills those same roles today. You may also see the Healthy Climate HCWHD4-100, a 100-pint whole-home unit sold through Lennox dealers, and 130-pint models from Anden, Aprilaire's industrial sister brand (see our [best Anden dehumidifier](/best/best-anden-dehumidifier/) guide).

For a true 100-pint dehumidifier, the **Aprilaire E100** is the one to buy. Step up to the **Aprilaire E130** for very large homes, choose the **Santa Fe Classic** for a big basement without ductwork, and save with the **AlorAir HDi90** if 90 pints will do. The **Aprilaire E080** is the smart pick when 80 pints is enough, and the **AlorAir Storm Elite** is the tool for flood recovery. Skip any portable that claims 80-plus pints without a DOE rating to back it up. Still weighing your options? Our [best whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) guide covers the full category.

faqs.a: Not in the mainstream portable sense. Under the DOE 2019 test, most portables top out around 50 pints. Units rated at 100 pints are whole-house or commercial machines rated under AHAM conditions, though some are freestanding and can be moved.

faqs.q: How big an area does a 100-pint dehumidifier cover?
faqs.a: It depends on the model and how damp the space is. The Aprilaire E100 is rated for up to about 5,500 square feet in a home, while the Santa Fe Classic is rated for basements up to about 2,700 square feet.

faqs.q: Is the Aprilaire E100 worth it?
faqs.a: For a large or damp home, yes. It replaces multiple portables, drains continuously, carries a five-year warranty and is among the most efficient whole-house units available. For a single small basement, a quality 50-pint portable with a pump may be enough.
The Aprilaire E080 is the best true 80-pint unit for whole-house or basement use. Be cautious with portables advertised as 80 pints; check whether the figure is a DOE rating or a saturation number.
Only for very large or very humid homes, or for drying out water damage. Most homes are well served by 80 to 100 pints. Oversizing wastes money and can cause short cycling.

faqs.q: How do I drain a 100-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Through a continuous drain: a gravity hose to a floor drain or sump, or a condensate pump that pushes water up and out. Units this size remove far too much water for a bucket.
